points: A terrible vision: the bones of the kings, Kohanim, nevi'im and people of Yerushalayim will be dug up and left under the sun, moon and stars they served, which can't help them.
Life will be so bad that people will choose death over life.

"Kulo shav bimrutzasam k'sus shotef bamilchamah": like the Mesillas Yesharim says, people run through life like a horse in battle and never stop to think. With all our technology and AI, we are busier than ever.
We need to stop and reflect, like on Yom Kippur and Shabbos. In a Sefer Torah, a missing gap between sections makes it invalid: the pauses matter as much as the writing.
"Mi yitein roshi mayim": Yirmiyahu, the most fire-and-brimstone navi, breaks down crying for his people. His rebuke comes from love, like Hashem who is with us in our pain.
